Overview / Our methodology

OUR METHODOLOGY · EDITORIAL STANDARDS

Every prediction should show its reasoning.

Pinoy Ball’s approach to explaining what could happen before an NBA game, and why. We examine team performance, player availability, tactical matchups and game conditions to form a reasoned view.

A prediction is a judgment under uncertainty. Our responsibility is to make the evidence, assumptions and limitations visible so readers can assess the conclusion for themselves.

01 · CORE FRAMEWORK

Our approach

We build every matchup preview around three core questions:

Question 1 Who has the advantage?

Identify the team with the stronger supporting evidence.

Question 2 What creates that advantage?

Explain the statistics, matchups and conditions that matter.

Question 3 What could change the outcome?

Present the opposing case, unresolved information and realistic upset scenarios.

The depth of each prediction depends on the quality of the available evidence. We distinguish what we have verified, what we infer and what remains unknown.

02 · DATA & VERIFICATION

Current data coverage

Each edition identifies the games covered, the sources consulted and when the information was retrieved.

Fixtures & start times

Checked against the official NBA schedule and public ESPN Scoreboard API, converted to Philippine Standard Time (UTC+8).

Records & statistics

Team win–loss records and performance metrics are attributed directly to their named sources and retrieval dates.

Injury & lineup verification

Player availability is treated as confirmed only when supported by an official injury report, team announcement or attributed reporting. An unavailable report never implies both teams are healthy.

Preliminary assessments

When a preview relies only on records, venue and limited historical context, we label it as a preliminary assessment rather than implying a full injury-adjusted analysis.

03 · SIX ANALYTICAL PILLARS

What we analyze

When evaluating an NBA matchup, we break the evidence into six distinct basketball topics:

Pillar 1

Team performance and recent form

We compare season-long performance with recent results to understand how each team is playing:

  • Offensive and defensive efficiency per 100 possessions.
  • Net rating and scoring margins.
  • Shooting efficiency and shot selection.
  • Turnover rates, offensive rebounding and free-throw generation.
  • Home and road performance, plus recent opponent quality.

A winning streak is supporting context, not a complete explanation. We assess whether results reflect repeatable strengths or hot shooting.

Pillar 2

Historical and head-to-head context

Previous meetings can reveal matchup patterns, depending on who played and how rosters changed:

  • How recent and comparable the previous meetings are.
  • Whether key players and coaching schemes remain involved.
  • Recurring advantages in scoring, rebounding or coverage.
  • Whether injuries or unusual circumstances shaped earlier games.

Older head-to-head results receive less weight when roster or tactical changes make them less representative.

Pillar 3

Player availability and rotation depth

A missing player changes how a lineup functions. We examine the role affected, not just scoring averages:

  • Confirmed absences and questionable statuses.
  • Reported minutes restrictions and return-to-play conditions.
  • Impact on ball handling, spacing, rim protection and rebounding.
  • Replacement quality, bench depth and likely closing lineups.

If a key player’s status is unresolved, we explain how the outlook shifts with and without that player.

Pillar 4

Tactical and individual matchups

We assess how each team’s strengths interact with the opponent’s specific weaknesses:

  • Interior scoring against rim protection.
  • Three-point creation against perimeter defense.
  • Pick-and-roll offense against likely defensive coverage.
  • Ball pressure vs. turnovers, board size and bench minutes.

Tactical conclusions are labeled as editorial analysis unless backed by directly attributed reporting or stats.

Pillar 5

Pace, possessions and scoring conditions

We examine the tempo and possession battle likely to shape the game:

  • Each team’s preferred pace and transition frequency.
  • Half-court execution, turnovers and second-chance points.
  • Shot distribution and reliance on three-point volume.
  • Which lineup is better positioned to dictate tempo.

We publish a projected score range only when a stated estimation method and sufficient data support it.

Pillar 6

Rest, travel and game context

We account for schedule spots that affect preparation, energy and rotations:

  • Back-to-back games and compressed multi-game stretches.
  • Rest advantages and recent starter minute loads.
  • Travel demands and home-court environment.
  • Confirmed rest plans and regular-season or playoff context.

Schedule context informs the read, but never automatically determines the pick.

04 · EDITORIAL WORKFLOW

How evidence becomes a prediction

Our editorial process follows a consistent eight-step sequence from verification to publication:

  1. Verify the game. Confirm the teams, venue, date and Philippine start time.
  2. Establish the performance baseline. Review available season statistics and recent form.
  3. Check comparability. Account for opponent quality, roster changes and sample size where the evidence allows.
  4. Assess availability. Review verified injury and lineup information, flagging unresolved statuses.
  5. Identify matchup advantages. Explain which statistical or tactical differences could influence the game.
  6. Test the opposing case. Identify the strongest reason the preferred team could lose.
  7. Choose a lean or no pick. Match the strength of the conclusion to the strength of the evidence.
  8. Publish the limitations. State missing information, important assumptions and conditions that could change the assessment.

Sources establish the underlying facts. Unless explicitly attributed to a documented model, the final selection is our editorial inference.

05 · PREVIEW ANATOMY

What every preview should show

Every Pinoy Ball matchup preview is organized into ten transparent components:

1. Game detailsTeams, venue and Philippine start time.
2. Publication statusWhen the analysis was published and last updated.
3. PredictionA reasoned lean or a no-pick decision.
4. Supporting evidenceThe most relevant verified facts and their implications.
5. Key matchupThe player, lineup or tactical contest likely to matter.
6. Availability statusConfirmed news and unresolved lineup questions.
7. Strongest counterargumentThe clearest case against our selection.
8. Upset scenarioA plausible path to victory for the opposing team.
9. LimitationsMissing data and factors not accounted for.
10. SourcesReferences and retrieval dates for material claims.
06 · CONFIDENCE TIERS

Confidence and no-pick decisions

We distinguish confidence in the available evidence from the numerical probability of a team winning:

Preliminary assessment

Important information is missing (such as game-day injury reports) or the available evidence is narrow.

Slight lean

The evidence favors one team, but meaningful uncertainty or strong counterarguments remain.

Stronger lean

Multiple relevant factors support the same team, with fewer unresolved issues. Remains a qualitative judgment.

No pick

The evidence is insufficient, conflicting or too dependent on unresolved information to support a useful selection.

These labels are qualitative descriptions, not numerical win probabilities, and do not imply measured historical accuracy.

07 · STATISTICAL STANDARDS

Statistical models and win probabilities

Qualitative editorial previews do not become model-based forecasts simply because they cite statistics.

We publish numerical win probabilities only when a documented forecasting method has been evaluated. Any model-based feature must explain:

  • Its inputs and treatment of missing data.
  • When predictions are generated prior to tip-off.
  • How it was tested on games outside its development sample.
  • How its performance compares with a simple baseline benchmark.
  • Whether its probabilities are calibrated over a meaningful sample size.
  • Its known limitations and revision history.

We do not invent confidence percentages or imply that simulations, injury adjustments or opponent-strength adjustments were performed when they were not.

08 · REVISION POLICY

Updates and late-breaking news

A prediction reflects the information verified at its publication time.

When verified pregame news materially changes an assessment, we:

  • Timestamp the update clearly on the preview page.
  • Identify the new information and its official or attributed source.
  • Explain how the update changes the matchup reasoning.
  • State explicitly whether the pick or confidence tier changed.
  • Preserve the original prediction and full revision history.
09 · TRACK RECORD

Results and accountability

Predictions remain reviewable after the final whistle in our results archive.

  • Permanent record: We preserve the original selection, publication timestamp, any pregame revisions and the verified final score.
  • Separate reporting: Correct picks, incorrect picks, pending games and no-pick decisions are tallied separately. No-pick decisions are never counted as wins or losses.
  • Transparent grading: Any accuracy summary must state the date range, number of graded picks and grading rules. Unsuccessful picks are never deleted.
  • Postgame review: We examine whether the underlying reasoning held up and which assumptions failed, knowing one win does not prove a method, and one loss does not disprove it.
10 · EDITORIAL ETHICS

Editorial independence

Pinoy Ball’s predictions are independent editorial judgments.

Commercial relationships never determine a selected winner or confidence label. Any sponsorship, affiliate arrangement or paid placement will be clearly disclosed alongside the relevant content. If market odds are referenced in the future, they will be timestamped and attributed with a clear separation between market prices and our editorial analysis.

Our goal is to earn readers’ trust through verifiable evidence, clear basketball reasoning and an honest record of results.
